figures.caption: Floor rounding selects cell (1,1) from the initial raw coordinates without changing the motion state.
figures.alt: Three annotated details at the initial floor-mode publication. Raw x and y are 320 and 448, representing 1.25 and 1.75 pixels. Velocities are 192 and 320, tick is zero and pixel ID is nine. One white cell is at column one, row one in the complete eight-by-eight image; the remaining cells are black.

figures.caption: Nearest rounding selects cell (1,2) from the same initial raw motion state.
figures.alt: Three annotated details at the initial nearest-mode publication. Only the rounding mode and derived pixel differ from the floor run. Raw state remains 320, 448, 192, 320 with tick zero. Pixel ID seventeen selects column one, row two; one white cell is visible in the complete eight-by-eight frame.

figures.caption: At tick five, the vertical overshoot has been reflected and the ball is traveling upward.
figures.alt: Three annotated details after the first vertical reflection in floor mode. Tick five publishes raw x 1280, y 1536, horizontal velocity 192 and vertical velocity minus 320. The complete eight-by-eight frame has one white cell at column five, row six, ID fifty-three. The model reflects the tentative y coordinate eight pixels around the seven-pixel wall to six pixels.

figures.caption: Native hexadecimal and signed-decimal views distinguish the wrapped word from the exact wider sum.
figures.alt: Three annotated details from the same overflow experiment replayed in two Debug launches. The next instruction is the overflow ready marker before exit reuses v0. Hexadecimal v0 is ffffffff80000100 and v1 is 0000000080000100. The native decimal view shows minus 2147483392 and positive 2147483904 respectively. Ordinary ball state is never initialized on this path.
